— Site information

Cookie & browser storage policy

Understand essential behavior, optional tracking categories, and the browser storage used to remember privacy preferences.

Review required before launch

This notice describes this website build. The owner must confirm the responsible contact, deployment regions, applicable law, provider arrangements, and any additional legal obligations before public launch.

Default configuration

This build has no configured analytics or advertising identifiers. It does not load optional Google or Meta tags by default. The site does not set its own HTTP cookies for reading pages. The hosting provider may use service-specific mechanisms; these must be reviewed against the deployed configuration.

Consent preference storage

The browser key ss-consent-v1 stores analytics and marketing choices, a version, and a timestamp for six months. It uses localStorage rather than a cookie. No name, email, message, or website form contents are stored in this key. If storage is unavailable, optional tracking stays off.

Analytics category

If configured, analytics supports measurement of website use and meaningful actions. Consent is denied by default. The exact vendor cookies, identifiers, duration, and purposes must be documented before enabling tags. GTM and direct GA4 are alternative deployment modes and must not duplicate collection.

Marketing category

If configured, marketing may support advertising measurement or audience features. It requires a separate permission. Google advertising consent states remain denied unless that category is allowed. A GTM container must be reviewed so custom and third-party tags follow the same rules.

Changing a choice

Open Privacy preferences in the footer to allow or decline optional categories. Declining a previously allowed category reloads the page with the denied state, preventing this implementation from loading the relevant tags again. It cannot erase information already received by a provider or reliably delete every provider cookie. Use browser controls and the actual provider tools where needed.

Before enabling integrations

Review applicable regional requirements, actual vendor behavior, retention, and user rights. Update this policy and the privacy notice to match the live services. Consent Mode v2 support is an implementation feature, not proof that all legal or tag configuration requirements have been met.
